record.observed_outcome: An independently constructed 97-byte BPI2 image declaring the maximum u64 nominal region count terminated the native checker with SIGABRT and an integer-overflow panic inside ArenaAllocator.

source_refs.summary: Exact malformed bytes, failing executable digest and observed native failure.
Malformed wire rejection and valid unused-name normalization regressions.

falsifying_evidence: 97-byte input sha256 7a781d4dd78b07a85ed7877c1c10824295f42a1fab38f6af2967a942fa024248 caused an allocator integer-overflow panic.
The numeric upper bound denotes available names, not a materialized collection length.
record.exclusion_rule: Do not size region indexes from the nominal region_count bound before canonicalization when sparse or unused names are admitted.
applicability_conditions: Region IDs are nominal u64 ordinals and region_count is their upper bound.
Untrusted wire or native logical inputs may carry sparse or unused names before canonical checking.
Temporary allocation width is derived from region_count rather than referenced region IDs.

reopening_criteria.condition: The index domain is derived from materialized/referenced regions and malformed maximum counts plus valid sparse/unused-name counterparts pass without an ordinal-sized allocation.

record.next_search_hint: Keep dense indexing for actual stored catalogs; use a sparse nominal-ID map where the integer is only a namespace bound.

reopening_criteria.condition: Successor transport preserves relative parameter order and inner binding scope order, demonstrated by independent effectful cleanup traces across native and both WASM embeddings without weakening normal-discard rejection.

record.hypothesis: Recompute all accumulated borrow queries before every lookup and settle function roots individually without excessive cost.
record.attempted_change: The incumbent resets Flow.changed on every settle call and requests a complete fixed point after each function root.
record.observed_outcome: A fixed 9576-byte image took median 89.46 ms native, 94.45 ms JavaScript and 67.26 ms Wasmtime for one run invocation. Reusing quiescent results and batching initial roots reduced these to 6.87, 5.61 and 5.16 ms over 21 samples with identical bytes. The full cross-engine source check completed in 51 seconds. All 546 prior conformance checks and the complete 2905986-byte record bundle remained identical.

source_refs.summary: Unconditional settlement and individually settled roots.
Raw samples, qualified native statistics, exact source hashes and complete conformance parity.
Permanent guards for allocation-free repeated queries, correct retry after interrupted settlement, and bounded growth across independent functions.

falsifying_evidence: Native CPU samples located the repeated work in borrow_flow.Flow.settle during output State admission.

The prior implementation fails the repeated-query allocation guard. Removing retry invalidation returns an incomplete source set. Restoring individual root settlement fails the allocation-growth guard.
record.exclusion_rule: Do not force a new global fixed point for unchanged borrow queries, or settle independent initial roots one at a time. Preserve invalidation on new queries, new facts and failed settlement.
applicability_conditions: Flow analyzes one immutable Program.
Every query or fact insertion marks changed.
Repeated public admission reuses the same accumulated query set within a Flow.

reopening_criteria.condition: New queries or facts, or an interrupted pass, require settlement; a measured replacement must retain those transitions and complete admission decisions.

record.next_search_hint: Use the existing dirty state with failure invalidation and batch known roots before evaluating their common fixed point.
